text: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.

This is what the LORD says: Look, waters are rising from the north; they will become a flooding torrent, sweeping over the land and all that fills it, over the city and those who live in it. The people will cry out, and everyone living in the land will wail.
At the sound of the pounding hooves of his stallions, at the roar of his chariots, the rumble of his wheels, fathers will not turn back for their children—their hands hang limp—

versions.text: At the sound of pounding hooves of stallions, at the roar of his chariots, the rumble of his wheels, fathers will not turn back for their children—their hands will hang limp—
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has the possessive suffix on "stallions" (אַבִּירָיו, "his stallions"), matching "his chariots" and "his wheels" later in the verse. Restoring it keeps the parallel structure. Also adding the article smooths the opening for oral reading, and "hang limp" as a present state reads more naturally in the interrupting clause.

text: because the day is coming to devastate all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every last ally. For the LORD is destroying the Philistines, the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor.

versions.text: because the day is coming to devastate all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every last ally. For the LORD is destroying the Philistines, the remnant from the coast of Caphtor.
versions.explanation: אִי means "coastland/island"; the construct is "the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor," not a remnant coming "from" the coast. The revised wording keeps the genitive relationship clear.

text: Gaza has shaved her head in mourning; Ashkelon lies silenced. You who remain in the valley, how long will you gash yourself?

versions.text: Gaza has shaved her head in mourning; Ashkelon lies silenced. You who remain in the valley, how long will you gash yourselves?
versions.explanation: The verb is second person feminine singular, and the address ("You who remain in the valley") is singular, so the plural reflexive "yourselves" creates a number mismatch.

text: Ah, sword of the LORD, how long until you rest? Return to your sheath; be still and quiet.
How can you rest, when the LORD has given the command? Against Ashkelon and against the seacoast—there he has appointed it.

versions.text: But how can it rest when the LORD has given it orders? Against Ashkelon and against the seacoast—there he has appointed it.
versions.explanation: The verb תִּשְׁקֹטִי is second person feminine singular, continuing the direct address to the sword begun in verse 6 ("how long until you rest?"). Shifting to "it" breaks the rhetorical continuity of the two verses; the third person appears only in the following clause (לָהּ), which the revision preserves.
